tb21_profile.skill: Recover the contents of a deleted file from a Linux filesystem (carve raw bytes / unallocated space / a running fd) and extract a string matching a strict format spec
tb21_profile.domain: Linux digital forensics: filesystem internals, deleted-inode/data recovery, byte-level string search under a known pattern
tb21_profile.task_form: recover/repair-corrupted-or-deleted-data, plus constrained-candidate search verified against a fixed password format

searches: tools.py search all 'memory dump|memdump|raw memory|/proc|swap|hexdump|strings command|grep .*raw|bounded by' -n 30
tools.py search tmax 'hardcoded|embedded (key|password|flag|string)|matching the pattern|of the form|formatted as|regex|regular expression' -n 30
tools.py search rts 'recover.*(credential|password|secret|key)|extract the password|crack|the password' -n 25
tools.py search rts 'validate .*password|password.*rules|matches the format|character password|password.*characters long' -n 15

TMax-15K.reason: Recover a specific named deleted file from a raw ext4 disk image - the exact deleted-file forensic recovery the TB2.1 task requires.
Recover an rm'd file from a still-running process's file descriptor via /proc; canonical Linux deleted-file recovery, same core skill.
Carve a deleted script from a raw memory dump and extract a key of a fixed form (SECRET_AUTH_KEY_<alnum>); recovery plus pattern-constrained extraction.
Recover deleted source (from .pyc) and brute-force a 4-char password of a known charset; recover-plus-constrained-guess, same two skills.
Scan raw bytes for magic markers then brute-force a 5-char password over a known alphabet - the byte-search and constrained-guess halves of the TB2.1 task.
Locate a hardcoded password inside a binary that must satisfy length and prefix constraints; find-a-string-matching-a-format transfers directly.
Recover a secret flag using a dump left by a crashed backup process; recovering a hidden secret from post-incident artifacts.
Identify a leaked credential from forensic evidence then audit for its use; recover-a-secret shape, different medium (audio).
Recover an old legacy password from leftover artifacts to decrypt a config; credential recovery, but no filesystem-level carving.
Recover an old credential as part of a rotation workflow; broad security-ops task, only the recover-a-credential step overlaps.

Reverse three crackme binaries to discover their passwords; password recovery from binaries, some by static analysis some by force.
Blind SQL-injection to extract a password; retrieves a secret but the mechanism is web exploitation, not file recovery.
Multi-stage steganography/forensics recovering a flag from JPEGs; extract-a-hidden-value shape, adjacent forensic subject matter.

Fix charset/language detection over varied byte inputs; the same problem of decoding raw bytes into readable strings.
Repair the ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentials grant; password-credential handling code, but a class-inheritance bug fix.
SecOC authenticator MAC verification returns wrong result; verifying a value against a computed hash, like checking a candidate password.
Fix a NameError in local zip handling; archive extraction plumbing, weak overlap with recovering data from a container.
Fix UTF-16BE detection with surrogate pairs; byte-level decoding correctness, adjacent to interpreting recovered raw bytes.
Fix ASN.1 binary decoding; parsing a structured binary format, the parse-raw-bytes skill that underlies carving.
Fix PDF binary parsing; extracting content from a binary container, loosely related to recovering data from raw bytes.
Fix SFTPClient.from_transport; secure-credential transport code, but nothing about recovery or constrained search.

Login lockout under a brute-force attack; the brute-force-against-a-credential domain, seen from the defender's side.
Add a flag to force fetching a password from the keyring; credential-retrieval handling, a feature-add rather than recovery.
KMS encrypt/decrypt behavior; cryptographic key handling, adjacent to decrypting recovered secrets.
KMS signing with PSS/SHA-256; hashing and signature verification, the compute-and-compare-a-hash primitive.
Fix basic-auth credential storage regression; credential handling code, no recovery or search component.
Traceback on requests unless an override password is set; password-gated request handling, a library bug fix.
Fix buzhash seed handling in a backup chunker; hashing over raw byte windows, distant relation to byte-level forensics.
OCSP IssuerNameHash/KeyHash handling; cryptographic hashing of identifiers, same crypto ecosystem, unrelated task shape.
Crash on a symlink pointing outside the root; filesystem-path edge case only, no credential or recovery relevance.

final_top10.reason: Recover a specific named deleted file from a raw ext4 image - identical to recovering deleted launchcode.txt from the /app filesystem.
Recover an rm'd file via a running process's open fd in /proc; canonical Linux deleted-file recovery, the exact core skill.
Recover a password from raw captured bytes and reconstruct its exact final form; recover-and-reconstruct a secret from unstructured data.
Carve a deleted script from a raw memory dump and extract a fixed-format key; recovery plus pattern-constrained string extraction.
Scan raw bytes for markers then brute-force a password over a known charset/length - the byte-search and constrained-guessing the TB2.1 task needs.
Recover deleted source from bytecode and crack a 4-char password of known charset; recover-deleted-data plus constrained guessing together.
Recover crackme passwords, the last by brute force since it is never stored; extract secrets not held in plaintext, with a bounded search.
Recover deleted credentials that are gone from the tree and identify the deleting commit; recover-a-deleted-secret with a forensics report.
Extract a password then validate it against all schema rules before writing it - mirrors checking a recovered password against a strict format.
Password-protected private key loading and decryption; the crypto/password-handling skill behind recovering a secret behind a passphrase.

notes: TMax-15K is by far the strongest pool: it has two literal deleted-file forensic-recovery tasks (ext4 image carve, and /proc fd recovery) plus several recover-plus-constrained-crack tasks, so the honest top of final_top10 is TMax-heavy. RTS's relevant items split into a recover-deleted-file-from-git-history family (transfer is real but the recovery is via VCS, not block-level) and a WebGoat 'extract tom's password then validate against schema' family (the validate-against-format half mirrors TB2.1's fixed-format check). SWE-Smith is genuinely weak here - I could not find defensible deleted-file/forensic recovery in it, so its ten are encoding-detection, zip-password, and binary-parsing bug fixes scored mostly 2; the merge step should treat SWE-Smith's contribution to this task as near-noise. SWE-Rebench's best is pyca cryptography (password-protected key), the rest are credential-handling bug fixes at overall 2. Strongest self-found finds not near the top of the shortlist: task_003280 (/proc fd recovery) and tw_18610 (pcap password reconstruction).
